items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: I can’t remember Tino’s last name but he was president of the New York local. He’s now the AFM president.

ctx.x: I know it was difficult. And when I was president I was elected to the international executive board and it’s like nine of us at that time telling everybody in the United States and Canada how they’re supposed to work under union contract. And the small locals didn’t like the large locals being part of that because we didn’t think like they did. And with me as president of the local in L.A. and Bill Moriarity the president of New York,

and Ed Ward, the president of Chicago we were big unions, they didn’t like that because they didn’t think we were thinking of them and yet we were telling them the music performance payment that you get to play your summer gigs from the Music Performance Trust Fund, that comes from musicians that record in New York, L.A., Chicago and Nashville. A certain amount of that money goes to create the Performance Fund. So you guys got that money by doing your concerts in the summertime. And so you know we aren’t here to…
I was talking to Tom Scott on an interview.
